messages:
Alex: Quick sync — sketching a rollback parity grid for hosted/dedicated/private interface changes. We need a lightweight plan that ensures: 1) safe rollback with no tenant data loss, 2) predictable failure domain, 3) minimal operator intervention. Thoughts?
Maya: +1. Can we start by categorizing changes as: control-plane-only, runtime-only, and cross-plane?
Jorge: Yep. Also add a fourth: config-schema-only (e.g., manifest surface). Those can often be feature-flagged.
Alex: Good call. Proposed rollback rules (very rough):
- control-plane-only: revert control-plane deployment, keep runtimes except when schema mismatch > X
- runtime-only: drain new runtime, fail open to previous variant
- cross-plane: coordinated two-step rollback: control-plane then runtime
- schema-only: on incompatible schema, reject new manifests and auto-rewrite minimal shim if possible
Maya: How do we ensure tenant routing doesn't flip to bad variants during rollback? Need affinity pinning or short-term sticky routing.
Priya: We should use a per-tenant routing token and TTL. On rollback, set TTL=0 for new variant and let existing pinned sessions finish. Ops can force cutover if needed.
Jorge: Also important: observable signals to trigger automated rollback. What metrics? Error rate, 95th latency spike, QoS degradation on success rate.
Alex: Proposed signal set: 1) token-level error rate > 2x baseline for 5m, 2) tail latency P99 > +200ms for 3m, 3) generation quality regression > threshold (from eval hooks). Any objections?
Maya: Those look reasonable. For quality regression we need promptset coverage per-tenant — we only have that for customers on Dedicated/Private with eval harnesses. Hosted customers? Canarying and human review.
Priya: On private deployments we can't run our centralized evals. Need local eval agents that report signed deltas to the control plane. Suggest `local-eval-agent` that posts hashes + summary.
Alex: Agreed. Add to the grid: who can trigger rollback (auto vs manual), visibility (dashboard + paging), and remediation playbook link.
Maya: Minor nit: ensure rollback playbooks include TTL on cache/batched requests to avoid prolonged degraded state (kv-cache invalidation steps).
Jorge: Example decision matrix snippet I threw together:
```
change_type,auto_rollback,manual_approval,affected_scope
control-plane,yes,no,global
runtime,no,yes,region/instance
schema,no,yes,tenant
cross-plane,conditional,yes,global+runtime
```
Priya: Looks good. Can we implement a kill-switch header for SDKs so clients can opt-out of auto-rollbacks during experiments?
Alex: We can add `X-RW-Rollback-Policy: opt_out|default|strict`. Add docs note and SDKs.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary job 3849990012 queued for runtime rollback test (staging).
Maya: Next steps: 1) formalize grid into a tiny RFC, 2) add metrics/alert runbook, 3) prototype local-eval-agent for Private. I can take the RFC draft.
Alex: Thanks Maya — please cc eng-oncall and product. I'll add the playbook skeleton and wire basic routing TTL change.
Priya: I'll prototype the header + SDK change and add tests for affinity pinning.
Jorge: I'll work on the observable signals integration (tracing + token-level SLOs).
Alex: Cool. We'll reconvene after RFC draft. :thumbsup:
